expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Stop trying to start. The re-reading is the diagnosis, not a discipline failure.
Ask what the first physical thing your hands would do. If there is no answer, the item is not a task.
If a decision is hidden inside it, extract the decision and make that the item.
Rewrite the item as the physical action, and leave the original phrasing next to it so the pattern is visible later.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Put yesterday's undone items in a separate place from today's plan. Never merge the two lists.
Give every carried item one of three dispositions: do today as a named block, reschedule to a named day, or drop.
Write the dropped items down as dropped. A deletion you can see is closure; a deletion you cannot see comes back as pressure.
Build today's plan only after the carried list is empty of undecided items.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Record one line per working day: the output that exists, in a form someone else could verify.
Never record effort, intent, or how it felt. Those go elsewhere if you want them.
Review weekly by reading the lines, not by remembering the week.
Draw exactly one conclusion per review, and change one thing.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Read your current state honestly and quickly: high, medium, or low. Do not negotiate with it.
Categorize your work the same way, in advance, so the matching does not require a decision when you are already low.
Take work from the matching category. A low block spent on low-category work is a productive block.
Note mismatches. Repeated mismatch at the same hour is a scheduling fact, not a discipline fact.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Do one physical, non-screen action first. It exists to move you out of bed-state, not to be virtuous.
Read one pre-written card that names today's first output. Deciding at 7am with no context is how the hour is lost.
Work the first block on that output before opening any queue: mail, messages, feeds, tickets.
Open the queues only after the block ends, and treat what is in them as input to the rest of the day rather than a re-plan.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Say the capacity out loud before you look at the list: what fraction of a normal day is actually available.
Pick exactly one output that would make today non-zero, and define its finished state in a sentence.
Delete or defer everything else in writing, so the deferral is a decision rather than a failure.
Stop when the one output is done, even if energy returns. Stopping on purpose is what makes the smaller day repeatable.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

Write the losing option's next review date so it is parked rather than abandoned.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: State the decision that is actually waiting, in one sentence ending in a verb.
List only what you already know that bears on it. New research is out of scope for the session.
Separate the list into facts, assumptions, and unknowns, and mark which unknowns would actually change the decision.
Make the decision, or name the single piece of information that would settle it and how you will get it.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Ask what you would own at the end, not what you would be paid during.

Ask what the worst realistic outcome costs, and whether you can carry that cost without it ending other things.

expected_structure.description: a structured list with at least three substantive items

items: Write down what evidence would tell you the current direction is wrong, in advance of looking for it.

If it has arrived, pivot deliberately and write down what you learned so the next attempt starts further along.
